zh.summary: 先以 User Story 表達角色與價值，再補齊功能、品質及約束，讓需求能對應具體情境與驗證。
objectives: 以角色、工作目標與理由撰寫一則 User Story。
分開功能、品質特性與設計約束，指出它們的關聯。
將模糊的好用、安全或快速改成可觀察條件或待確認事項。

readingGuide.goal: 以角色、工作目標與理由撰寫一則 User Story。
readingGuide.startingPoint: spec.md 工作表與合成收件案例；不需要安裝測試工具。
readingGuide.route: 先看情境與原理，再比較例子，最後擴寫 spec.md 並用檢核題自查。
readingGuide.output: spec.md 具有Story、功能／品質／約束、情境連結與待確認事項。

sections.heading: 把使用者想法變成可驗證的規格
paragraphs: 這一章是「規格驅動軟體開發」（Specification-Driven Development, SDD）的重要基礎。
今天最重要的一句話：使用者告訴你他想解決什麼問題，不代表你已經知道軟體應該怎麼做，更不代表你知道怎樣才算完成。
這就是為什麼軟體工程需要區分四件事：

- User Story（使用者故事）： 誰需要這個東西？他想完成什麼？為什麼？
- Functional Requirements（功能需求，FR）： 系統具體要做哪些事情？
- Non-Functional Requirements（非功能需求，NFR）： 系統做這些事情時，應該具備什麼品質？
- Constraints（約束條件）： 開發與使用過程中，有哪些限制不能違反？

sections.heading: 一、先從餐廳點餐理解這四件事
paragraphs: 假設你準備開一家餐廳，想委託廚師幫你設計午餐。
你對廚師說：
「我希望上班族中午可以吃到一份健康、方便、快速的午餐。」
這個需求有錯嗎？
沒有。可是廚師會遇到很多問題：
要提供哪些餐點？什麼叫健康？多快才算快速？客人有沒有食物過敏？價格有沒有限制？
因此，我們必須逐步把模糊的想法轉成可以執行的要求。

blocks.caption: 圖 1｜把午餐想法轉成可驗證的要求
blocks.description: 箭頭表示需求逐步具體化；FR 與 NFR 並列，分別說明行為與品質，並非先後步驟。此為教學示意，品質條件仍須具體化。

items.title: User Story｜我為什麼需要它？
items.body: 上班族希望午休能快速吃到合適的餐點，以便準時回去工作

items.title: FR｜要做什麼？
items.body: 提供點餐、客製化、付款與訂單查詢

items.title: NFR｜做得如何？
items.body: 流程易懂、回應穩定、操作方便

items.title: Constraints｜有哪些限制？
items.body: 遵守已確認的食材限制、預算及設備條件

items.title: Acceptance Criteria｜如何確認有做到？
items.body: 指定情境下能正確點餐、處理過敏限制、完成付款與查詢；品質指標也經過測試

paragraphs: 這個流程的關鍵不在文件名稱，而在於逐步減少歧義，讓不同人可以對「完成」有相同理解。
餐廳廚師、軟體工程師、AI Coding Agent，面對模糊需求時都會有同樣的困難：如果沒有明確要求，就只能自己猜。

sections.heading: 二、User Story：先說清楚使用者的真正目的
paragraphs: User Story 常見的表達方式是：
> 身為某種使用者（As a），我希望能夠完成某件事（I want），以便獲得某種價值（So that）。
我們從不同產業來看：

blocks.caption: 表 2
rows: 醫療
身為護理師，我希望給藥前能查看病人的過敏紀錄，以降低用藥風險。
電商
身為消費者，我希望結帳前知道運費，以便決定是否購買。
教育
身為學生，我希望看到自己常答錯的觀念，以便安排複習。
金融
身為徵信人員，我希望快速找出報告缺少的資料，以便完成審核準備。
製造
身為產線主管，我希望及時知道設備異常，以便安排檢查，減少停機。

paragraphs: 仔細看，這些故事都沒有先指定 Python、React、資料庫或 AI 模型。
為什麼？
因為 User Story 首先回答的是使用者價值（User Value），而不是工程師要使用哪個工具。
例如，「學生希望知道自己的弱點」可以透過錯題列表、能力圖、推薦複習清單等方式實現，不一定需要 AI。
### 最常見的錯誤
「身為使用者，我希望畫面有一個藍色按鈕，以便按下它。」
這句話雖然套用了 Story 句型，但沒有真正說明使用者的工作目的。
更好的寫法是：
「身為收件人員，我希望提交資料前能檢查必要欄位，以免將不完整的資料交給下一個處理者。」
至於是否用藍色按鈕來實現，通常是後續設計問題。
還要注意：User Story 是溝通和需求探索的起點，不是完整規格，也不需要把所有需求都硬塞進固定句型。

sections.heading: 三、功能需求（FR）：系統到底要做什麼？
paragraphs: 假設你準備開發一個醫院掛號系統。
你收到的 User Story 是：
「身為病人，我希望能在線上掛號，以便不必親自到醫院排隊。」
這段話有說明價值，但沒有告訴工程師完整的工作規則。
功能需求就是將它進一步拆解，例如：

blocks.caption: 表 3
rows: FR-01
病人可以查詢可預約門診
指定日期後顯示可預約診次
FR-02
病人可以預約仍有名額的診次
預約成功後產生預約紀錄
FR-03
病人可以取消自己的預約
取消後狀態正確更新
FR-04
額滿的診次不得再接受一般預約
模擬額滿後確認無法超額預約

paragraphs: 功能需求不只描述「系統應該允許什麼」，也要描述「系統應該拒絕什麼」。
例如，醫院剩下一個掛號名額，卻有兩個病人同時按下預約。
系統不能因為兩個人都看到還有名額，就同時接受兩筆預約，除非院方明確允許超額掛號。
因此，規格還要回答同時操作、資料更新、錯誤處理等問題。
這也是為什麼只讓 AI「做出線上掛號功能」遠遠不夠。

sections.heading: 四、非功能需求（NFR）：功能能用，不代表系統好用
paragraphs: 想像有兩家銀行提供相同的網路轉帳功能。

blocks.caption: 圖 2｜相同轉帳功能，不同品質
blocks.description: 兩家銀行是合成比較案例；卡片並列比較品質，不表示時間或因果。避免重複扣款也需要具體功能與規則來實現。

items.title: 銀行 A
items.body:
功能存在，但品質欠佳
轉帳常需要等待很久，偶爾當機，錯誤訊息不清楚。

items.title: 銀行 B
items.body:
功能與品質都經過設計
回應時間可預期，失敗時狀態清楚，能避免重複扣款。

paragraphs: 兩家銀行都能提供轉帳，但使用體驗與風險不同。
這就是非功能需求的重要性。
常見品質面向包括：

blocks.caption: 表 4
rows: Performance 效能
做事要多快
查詢大量資料時，回應時間在約定門檻內
Reliability 可靠性
能否持續正確運作
服務中斷後，交易狀態仍正確
Accessibility 可近用性
不同能力的人能否操作
不使用滑鼠也能完成主要工作
Usability 易用性
操作是否容易理解
使用者清楚知道怎麼修正錯誤
Maintainability 可維護性
未來能否容易修改
新增欄位不必大幅修改其他功能
Security 安全性
能否防止不當存取與操作
未授權者無法讀取他人紀錄

sections.heading: 為什麼「系統要很快」不是好的需求？
paragraphs: 假設你委託工程師製作購物網站。
你說：「這個網站一定要很快。」
工程師回覆：「完成了，我覺得很快。」
你怎麼證明他有沒有達成？
沒有辦法。因為你們對「快」沒有共同定義。
我們可以採用以下方式將要求具體化：

blocks.caption: 圖 3｜把「很快」寫成可以量測的條件
blocks.description: 上下兩段比較需求的具體程度；50 人、95% 與 2 秒均為示範，必須經情境、負載、成本與利害關係人確認。

items.title: 模糊需求
items.body: 「商品搜尋要很快。」

items.title: 可驗證需求的寫法（示範數值，尚非正式門檻）
items.body: 「在指定測試設備、固定資料集與 50 位模擬同時使用者的條件下，從伺服器收到搜尋請求到回傳完整結果，95% 的請求應在 2 秒內完成。」

paragraphs: 這裡的 95% 通常可以用 p95 latency（第 95 百分位延遲）表達。
但為什麼要用 50 人、2 秒？
這些數字必須經過使用情境、負載測試、成本與利害關係人確認，不能隨便填入，就當作正式需求。
如果還沒有證據，正確做法是留下待確認事項（TBR，To Be Resolved），明確指定誰來確認、何時確認，以及要蒐集哪些量測資料。
NASA 的需求工程指引強調需求必須清楚、一致、可追溯、可驗證，並避免單獨使用「快速、容易、安全」這類無法直接檢驗的形容詞。

sections.heading: 五、Constraints：有哪些不能跨越的界線？
paragraphs: 約束條件不一定是系統功能，也不完全等同品質。
例如你正在做一套學校的學生資料分析系統。
校方可能要求：
「第一階段只能用去識別化測試資料，不准連正式學生資料庫。」
這代表即使你做出非常好的資料分析功能，只要直接連到正式資料庫，就違反了這一階段的要求。
其他例子包括必須在離線環境執行、只能使用指定硬體、預算不得超過核准額度，或不得把特定資料傳送給外部服務。
要特別注意，FR、NFR、Constraints 並不是完全互斥的三個盒子。
例如「只有經授權的醫師才能查看指定病歷」，可以拆成具體的存取控制功能、授權判斷規則、稽核要求與資料治理約束。
分類只是幫助團隊討論；真正重要的是每個條件都能夠被理解、實作與驗證。

sections.heading: 六、最重要的實作：把四種需求整合成一份規格
paragraphs: 現在回到教材的合成收件資料案例。
假設你要開發一套收件系統，收件人員會收到包含姓名、案件編號與聯絡方式的測試資料。
我們從最初的 User Story 一步步寫到可以驗收的規格。

blocks.caption: 圖 4｜一個故事與四條規格
blocks.description: 代號供追溯與驗收引用；五列是不同規格角色，不表示五個執行步驟，也不代表已實作或通過測試。

items.title: S-01｜User Story
items.body: 身為收件人員，我希望在匯出前知道哪些必要欄位沒有填寫，以便補齊後再交接。

items.title: FR-01｜檢查缺漏
items.body: 必要欄位不存在、為空字串或只有空白字元時，系統應將它列為缺漏。

items.title: FR-02｜防止錯誤匯出
items.body: 未通過完整性檢查時，不得產生標示為「完整」的匯出報告。

items.title: NFR-01｜鍵盤可操作性
items.body: 使用者應能只用鍵盤完成填寫、檢查、修正與匯出；操作焦點必須可辨識，且不應陷入無法離開的操作區域。

items.title: C-01｜資料與使用範圍
items.body: 本次原型只處理合成資料，採單人本機操作，不連接真實收件系統，也不宣稱具有正式業務受理能力。

paragraphs: 這裡對應的 W3C WCAG 2.2 鍵盤操作原則，要求一般功能可以透過鍵盤介面操作；但只寫下這條規格，不代表產品已通過可近用性測試。

sections.heading: 下一步：把需求連到驗收測試
paragraphs: 我們以 FR-01 與 FR-02 為例，寫出兩種情境。
正常情境：

blocks.heading: 正常情境
paragraphs: 以下文字供規格練習與驗收討論；實際結果另行記錄。
雙語頁面保留相同原始規格文字；英文頁另附逐項翻譯。
blocks.code:
Given 所有必要欄位都已完整填寫
When 使用者按下「檢查」
Then 系統顯示檢查通過
And 允許匯出完整報告

paragraphs: 異常情境：

blocks.heading: 異常情境
paragraphs: 以下文字供規格練習與驗收討論；實際結果另行記錄。
雙語頁面保留相同原始規格文字；英文頁另附逐項翻譯。
blocks.code:
Given 案件編號只有空白字元
When 使用者按下「檢查」
Then 系統指出案件編號缺漏
And 不允許匯出完整報告

paragraphs: 這種 Given／When／Then 的寫法，就是下一章 M05-03 要深入學習的驗收情境表達方式。
還有一個容易遺漏的情境：
假設你剛剛完成檢查，之後又把案件編號刪掉，系統能不能直接沿用先前的檢查通過結果？
不應該。因為資料已經改變，舊結果可能失效。
因此還需要補充規則：資料修改後，既有的完整性檢查結果必須失效，重新檢查通過後才能完整匯出。
這正是軟體工程真正困難的地方：問題常常不是程式不會寫，而是需求沒有把例外與狀態變化想清楚。

sections.heading: 七、為什麼這件事在 AI Coding Agent 時代更重要？
paragraphs: 過去你找工程師開發軟體，工程師可能會主動追問需求。
現在你可以直接告訴 AI：
「幫我做一個資料檢查網站。」
AI 可能很快產生一個漂亮、可以操作的網站，但它可能沒有正確處理空白欄位、過期檢查結果、匯出限制，甚至沒有定義何謂完整。
所以正確的 AI 協作流程應是：

blocks.caption: 圖 5｜依規格進行 AI 協作
blocks.description: 編號表示協作順序；需求變更時回到相關規格與測試重新確認。AI 的完成回覆仍需實際測試證據。

items.title: 先寫 User Story
items.body: 確認使用者與目的。

items.title: 補 FR、NFR、Constraints
items.body: 定義功能、品質及界線。

items.title: 補 Acceptance Criteria
items.body: 寫出正常、錯誤及邊界情境。

items.title: 交給 AI Coding Agent 實作
items.body: 要求依照規格開發，不自行假定重要業務規則。

items.title: 執行測試並保留證據
items.body: 檢查結果是否符合需求，未測試的項目不得宣稱通過。

paragraphs: 每一個需求最好都有穩定編號，能追溯到相應的驗收情境及測試結果。例如：
`S-01 → FR-01 → AC-01 → TEST-01 → PASS / FAIL`
這叫做 Traceability（可追溯性）。
將來需求改變時，你可以知道哪條規格要更新、哪些測試要重跑，而不是只憑 AI 說「已修改完成」。這也是 NASA 需求指引強調的核心特性之一。

sections.heading: 八、動手練習：寫一份最小規格
paragraphs: 本章不需要先寫程式。可以使用 `spec.md` 記錄如下內容：

blocks.heading: 規格模板
paragraphs: 以下文字供規格練習與驗收討論；實際結果另行記錄。
雙語頁面保留相同原始規格文字；英文頁另附逐項翻譯。
blocks.code:
# S-01 使用者故事
角色：
目標：
理由：

# Functional Requirements
FR-01：
FR-02：

# Non-Functional Requirements
NFR-01：

# Constraints
C-01：

# Acceptance Criteria
AC-01 正常情境：
AC-02 異常情境：

# Verification
驗證方法：
實際結果：待驗

# Open Questions
尚待確認的規則：
確認負責人：

paragraphs: 建議先選一個很小的業務工作，而不是一口氣規劃整套大型系統。完成規格後，應能讓另一位工程師或另一個 AI Agent 根據同一份內容，產出外部行為一致、可以獨立驗收的系統。

sections.heading: 九、理解檢核
paragraphs: 以下是三個情境題。先自行判斷，再展開參考解析；本頁不提交答案，也不據此判定學習完成。
本章最值得記住的結論是：User Story 定義價值，FR 定義行為，NFR 定義品質，Constraints 定義界線，而 Acceptance Criteria 讓這一切變得可以驗證。

exercise.environment: spec.md 工作表與合成收件案例；不需要安裝測試工具。
steps: 撰寫一則收件人員故事，確認角色、工作結果與理由都有出現。
補兩條功能需求、一條品質要求及一條本版約束，為每條指定驗證方法與狀態。
把「快速」改寫成需要確認的量測條件，核對至少一條功能可連到正常與負向情境，再請同儕找缺口或自行逐項檢查。
exercise.expected: spec.md 具有Story、功能／品質／約束、情境連結與待確認事項。
exercise.check: 條款可觀察且不靠句型充數；未確認門檻與未執行結果沒有被填成通過。
exercise.cleanup: 保留合成標記、來源與決策角色；移除沒有依據的百分比、時間或正式規定宣稱。

en.summary: Use a User Story to express role and value, then add functions, qualities and constraints connected to concrete scenarios and verification.
objectives: Write a User Story with role, work goal and reason.
Separate functional requirements, quality attributes and design constraints while identifying their relationships.
Replace vague usability, security or speed claims with observable conditions or explicit unknowns.

readingGuide.goal: Write a User Story with role, work goal and reason.
readingGuide.startingPoint: The spec.md worksheet and synthetic intake case; no testing-tool installation is needed.
readingGuide.route: Read the situation and principles, compare examples, then expand spec.md and use the checks to review your understanding.
readingGuide.output: spec.md with a story, functional/quality/constraint clauses, scenario links and pending questions.

sections.heading: Turn a user idea into a verifiable specification
paragraphs: This chapter provides a foundation for Specification-Driven Development (SDD).
A user explaining the problem they want to solve does not yet tell you exactly how the software should behave or how to establish completion.
Software engineering therefore distinguishes four things:

- User Story: Who needs this, what are they trying to accomplish, and why?
- Functional Requirements (FR): What specific things must the system do?
- Non-Functional Requirements (NFR): What qualities must the system have while doing them?
- Constraints: What restrictions must development and use respect?

sections.heading: 1. Understand the distinctions through ordering lunch
paragraphs: Suppose you are opening a restaurant and ask a chef to design lunch.
You say:
“I want office workers to have a healthy, convenient and quick lunch.”
Is anything wrong with that request?
No. But the chef still has questions:
What meals should be available? What counts as healthy? How quick is quick? Do customers have food allergies? Is there a price limit?
We need to turn a broad idea into actionable requirements.

blocks.caption: Figure 1 | Turn a lunch idea into verifiable requirements
blocks.description: Arrows mean increasing specificity. FR and NFR are parallel behavior and quality concerns, not sequential steps. This teaching illustration still requires more specific quality conditions.

items.title: User Story | Why do I need it?
items.body: Office workers want a suitable meal during their lunch break so that they can return to work on time.

items.title: FR | What should it do?
items.body: Provide ordering, customization, payment and order lookup.

items.title: NFR | How well should it work?
items.body: The process should be understandable, responses dependable and operation convenient.

items.title: Constraints | What restrictions apply?
items.body: Respect confirmed ingredient restrictions, budget and equipment conditions.

items.title: Acceptance Criteria | How can we confirm it works?
items.body: In specified scenarios, customers can order correctly, handle allergy restrictions, pay and look up orders; quality measures are also tested.

paragraphs: The purpose is to reduce ambiguity so that different people share an understanding of completion, regardless of document names.
Chefs, software engineers and AI Coding Agents face the same difficulty with vague requests: without explicit requirements, they have to guess.

sections.heading: 2. User Story: establish the user's actual purpose
paragraphs: A common User Story format is:
> As a particular kind of user, I want to accomplish something, so that I obtain a particular value.
Consider examples from different industries:

blocks.caption: Table 2
rows: Healthcare
As a nurse, I want to see a patient's allergy record before administering medication, so that I can reduce medication risks.
Commerce
As a shopper, I want to know shipping costs before checkout, so that I can decide whether to buy.
Education
As a student, I want to see concepts I frequently get wrong, so that I can plan revision.
Finance
As a credit reviewer, I want to find missing information in a report quickly, so that I can prepare the review.
Manufacturing
As a production supervisor, I want timely notice of equipment anomalies, so that I can arrange inspection and reduce downtime.

paragraphs: None of these stories starts by specifying Python, React, a database or an AI model.
Why?
A User Story first expresses user value rather than the engineer's tool choice.
For example, students could identify weaknesses through a list of errors, a capability map or a revision list. AI is not necessarily required.
### A common mistake
“As a user, I want a blue button on the screen, so that I can press it.”
This follows the sentence pattern but does not explain the user's work purpose.
A better version is:
“As an intake worker, I want to check required fields before submitting information, so that I do not hand incomplete data to the next person.”
Whether a blue button implements this is usually a later design decision.
A User Story starts communication and requirements exploration. It is not a complete specification, and not every requirement needs to fit this sentence pattern.

sections.heading: 3. Functional requirements: what exactly must the system do?
paragraphs: Suppose you are developing a hospital appointment system.
You receive this User Story:
“As a patient, I want to book an appointment online, so that I do not have to queue at the hospital.”
It explains value but does not give the engineer all the operating rules.
Functional requirements make the request more specific:

blocks.caption: Table 3
rows: FR-01
Patients can look up clinics with available appointments.
Selecting a date displays bookable sessions.
FR-02
Patients can book a session with remaining capacity.
A successful booking creates an appointment record.
FR-03
Patients can cancel their own appointments.
Cancellation updates the status correctly.
FR-04
Full sessions must reject ordinary additional bookings.
Simulate a full session and confirm that capacity cannot be exceeded.

paragraphs: Functional requirements describe both what the system permits and what it rejects.
For example, two patients may press Book at the same time when only one appointment remains.
The system must not accept both simply because both patients saw available capacity, unless the hospital explicitly permits overbooking.
The specification therefore also needs to address concurrent actions, data updates and error handling.
Asking AI only to “build online booking” leaves these rules unresolved.

sections.heading: 4. Non-functional requirements: working functionality still needs quality
paragraphs: Imagine two banks offering the same online transfer function.

blocks.caption: Figure 2 | The same transfer function with different quality
blocks.description: These banks are a synthetic comparison. Parallel cards compare quality, without implying time or causality. Preventing duplicate debits also requires specific functions and rules.

items.title: Bank A
items.body:
The function exists, but quality is poor.
Transfers often take a long time, the service occasionally crashes, and error messages are unclear.

items.title: Bank B
items.body:
Both functionality and quality have been designed.
Response times are predictable, failure states are clear, and duplicate debits can be prevented.

paragraphs: Both banks offer transfers, but the experience and risks differ.
That is why non-functional requirements matter.
Common quality dimensions include:

blocks.caption: Table 4
rows: Performance
How quickly work happens
Queries over a large dataset meet an agreed response-time threshold.
Reliability
Whether correct operation continues
Transaction states remain correct after service interruption.
Accessibility
Whether people with different abilities can operate it
The main task can be completed without a mouse.
Usability
Whether operation is understandable
Users understand how to correct an error.
Maintainability
Whether later changes are manageable
Adding a field does not require extensive changes to unrelated functions.
Security
Whether improper access and actions are prevented
Unauthorized people cannot read someone else's records.

sections.heading: Why is “the system must be fast” a poor requirement?
paragraphs: Suppose you commission a shopping website.
You say, “This website must be fast.”
The engineer replies, “Done. It feels fast to me.”
How would you establish whether the requirement was met?
You cannot, because there is no shared definition of fast.
Make it concrete:

blocks.caption: Figure 3 | Make “fast” measurable
blocks.description: The two rows compare specificity. The 50 users, 95% and 2 seconds are illustrative; confirm them against the scenario, load, costs and stakeholder needs.

items.title: Vague requirement
items.body: “Product search must be fast.”

items.title: Verifiable wording: illustrative values, not an approved threshold
items.body: “On specified test equipment, with a fixed dataset and 50 simulated concurrent users, 95% of requests should finish within 2 seconds, measured from the server receiving a search request to returning the complete result.”

paragraphs: The 95% condition can usually be expressed using p95 latency, the 95th-percentile latency.
But why choose 50 users and 2 seconds?
These figures require confirmation against the usage scenario, load tests, costs and stakeholder needs. Inserting arbitrary numbers does not make them official requirements.
Where evidence is missing, record a TBR (To Be Resolved) item, identify who will resolve it and when, and state which measurements are needed.
NASA's requirements guidance emphasizes clarity, consistency, traceability and verifiability, and warns against undefined terms such as fast, easy or safe.

sections.heading: 5. Constraints: which boundaries must be respected?
paragraphs: A constraint is not necessarily a function and is not identical to quality.
Suppose you are building a school student-data analysis system.
The school might require:
“Phase one may use only de-identified test data and must not connect to the production student database.”
Even an excellent analysis function violates this phase's requirements if it connects directly to that database.
Other examples include offline execution, specified hardware, an approved budget limit, or a ban on sending particular data to external services.
FR, NFR and constraints are not completely separate boxes.
For example, “Only authorized doctors can view specified medical records” can be decomposed into access-control functions, authorization rules, audit requirements and data-governance constraints.
Classification supports discussion. Every condition still needs to be understood, implemented and verified.

sections.heading: 6. Integrate the requirements into one specification
paragraphs: Return to the course's synthetic intake-data example.
Suppose an intake system receives test records containing a name, case number and contact information.
Develop the original User Story into a specification that can be accepted.

blocks.caption: Figure 4 | One story and four specification clauses
blocks.description: Identifiers support traceability and acceptance references. These rows are specification roles, not execution steps or evidence of implementation or passed tests.

items.title: S-01 | User Story
items.body: As an intake worker, I want to know which required fields are missing before export, so that I can complete them before handoff.

items.title: FR-01 | Check omissions
items.body: If a required field is absent, an empty string or whitespace only, the system shall list it as missing.

items.title: FR-02 | Prevent incorrect export
items.body: If completeness checking has not passed, the system shall not produce an export report labelled “complete.”

items.title: NFR-01 | Keyboard operation
items.body: Users shall be able to fill in, check, correct and export using only the keyboard. Focus must be identifiable and must not become trapped in an area they cannot leave.

items.title: C-01 | Data and usage scope
items.body: This prototype processes only synthetic data, runs locally for one person, does not connect to a real intake system and does not claim official business intake capability.

paragraphs: The corresponding WCAG 2.2 keyboard principles require ordinary functionality to be keyboard operable. Writing the requirement does not establish that the product has passed accessibility testing.

sections.heading: Next: connect requirements to acceptance tests
paragraphs: For FR-01 and FR-02, write two scenarios.
Normal scenario:

blocks.heading: Normal scenario
paragraphs: This text supports specification practice and acceptance discussion; record actual results separately.

Given all required fields are complete
When the user selects Check
Then the system displays a passed check
And permits export of a complete report
blocks.code:
Given 所有必要欄位都已完整填寫
When 使用者按下「檢查」
Then 系統顯示檢查通過
And 允許匯出完整報告

paragraphs: Error scenario:

blocks.heading: Error scenario
paragraphs: This text supports specification practice and acceptance discussion; record actual results separately.

Given the case number contains only whitespace
When the user selects Check
Then the system identifies the missing case number
And does not permit export of a complete report
blocks.code:
Given 案件編號只有空白字元
When 使用者按下「檢查」
Then 系統指出案件編號缺漏
And 不允許匯出完整報告

paragraphs: The next chapter, M05-03, develops this Given/When/Then style of acceptance scenarios.
There is another easily missed scenario:
After a successful check, suppose you delete the case number. Can the system continue using the earlier passed result?
It should not. The changed data may invalidate that result.
Add a rule: changing data invalidates the existing completeness-check result. A complete export requires a new successful check.
Software engineering often becomes difficult because exceptions and state changes have not been specified, even when writing the code itself is straightforward.

sections.heading: 7. Why does this matter more with AI Coding Agents?
paragraphs: A human engineer may ask follow-up questions when you request software.
Now you can directly ask AI:
“Build me a data-checking website.”
AI may quickly create an attractive, operable site while mishandling whitespace-only fields, stale check results or export restrictions. It may never define completeness.
A useful AI collaboration process is:

blocks.caption: Figure 5 | Collaborate with AI using a specification
blocks.description: Numbers indicate collaboration order. Changed requirements require revisiting the relevant specification and tests. An AI completion message still requires executed test evidence.

items.title: Write a User Story
items.body: Establish the user and purpose.

items.title: Add FR, NFR and constraints
items.body: Define behavior, quality and boundaries.

items.title: Add Acceptance Criteria
items.body: Cover normal, error and boundary scenarios.

items.title: Ask an AI Coding Agent to implement
items.body: Follow the specification and do not invent consequential business rules.

items.title: Execute tests and retain evidence
items.body: Compare results against requirements and leave untested items unverified.

paragraphs: Give requirements stable identifiers so they can link to acceptance scenarios and test results. For example:
`S-01 → FR-01 → AC-01 → TEST-01 → PASS / FAIL`
This is traceability.

When requirements change, the links identify which specifications to update and tests to rerun, beyond relying on AI's “changes complete” message. Traceability is also a central feature of NASA's requirements guidance.

sections.heading: 8. Practice: write a minimal specification
paragraphs: You do not need to write code for this chapter. Record the following in `spec.md`:

blocks.heading: Specification template
paragraphs: This text supports specification practice and acceptance discussion; record actual results separately.

# Open Questions

paragraphs: Choose one small business task before planning a large system. The specification should allow another engineer or AI Agent to produce externally consistent behavior that can be independently accepted.

sections.heading: 9. Check your understanding
paragraphs: Judge each scenario before opening its reference explanation. This page does not submit answers or establish learning completion.
A User Story defines value, FR defines behavior, NFR defines quality, constraints define boundaries, and Acceptance Criteria make those conditions verifiable.

exercise.environment: The spec.md worksheet and synthetic intake case; no testing-tool installation is needed.
steps: Write an intake-worker story containing role, work outcome and reason.
Add two functional requirements, one quality requirement and one version constraint, each with a verification method and status.
Replace “fast” with measurement conditions needing confirmation. Link at least one function to normal and negative cases, then have a peer find gaps or review each item yourself.
exercise.expected: spec.md with a story, functional/quality/constraint clauses, scenario links and pending questions.
exercise.check: Clauses are observable rather than template filler. Unconfirmed thresholds and unexecuted results are not marked passed.
exercise.cleanup: Keep synthetic labels, sources and decision roles. Remove unsupported percentages, times or claims of official rules.

zh.prompt: 某主管說：「我要一套好用又安全的人事系統。」目前最欠缺的是什麼？
options: 指定使用哪一種前端框架
補充使用者目的、具體行為、品質條件、約束與驗收方式
先讓 AI 把全部畫面做出來
把句子改寫成英文
rationales: 前端框架是實作選擇，無法補足使用者目的與驗收規則。
B：先確認目的、行為、品質、約束與驗收，才有共同的完成條件。
畫面只能展示部分介面，不能替代授權、資料與品質規則。
語言轉換不會自動補齊模糊需求。

en.prompt: A manager says, “I need a usable and secure HR system.” What is most missing?
options: A chosen frontend framework
The user's purpose, concrete behavior, quality conditions, constraints and acceptance method
Having AI build all screens first
Rewriting the request in English
rationales: A frontend framework is an implementation choice and does not establish purpose or acceptance rules.
B: Establish purpose, behavior, quality, constraints and acceptance to share a definition of completion.
Screens demonstrate only part of an interface, without establishing authorization, data or quality rules.
Translation does not automatically resolve vague requirements.

zh.prompt: 系統必須禁止員工查看其他部門的機密紀錄。這比較適合如何處理？
options: 只要放在非功能需求即可，不必測試
只要有登入畫面就已完成
寫出授權規則與拒絕行為，並設計測試驗證
只需要加密資料庫
rationales: 分類不會免除驗證責任；拒絕未授權存取需要實測。
登入回答身分，授權仍要判斷該身分可以讀哪些資料。
C：明確定義角色、部門、紀錄範圍與拒絕行為，再驗證允許與拒絕情境。
加密保護資料的特定層面，無法單獨決定誰有權讀取。

en.prompt: The system must prevent employees from viewing another department's confidential records. How should this be handled?
options: Put it only under NFR and omit tests
Treat a login screen as completion
Define authorization rules and rejection behavior, then verify them with tests
Only encrypt the database
rationales: Classification does not remove verification duties; unauthorized-access rejection needs testing.
Login establishes identity; authorization still determines which records that identity may read.
C: Specify roles, departments, record scope and rejection behavior, then test both allowed and denied cases.
Encryption protects particular aspects of data but does not alone determine who may read it.

zh.prompt: AI 已根據規格產生程式碼，並表示所有功能都已完成。接下來最合理的作法是？
options: 直接上線
只確認畫面是否美觀
逐項執行對應的正常、異常與品質驗收，記錄測試證據
改成另一個 AI 模型重新生成
rationales: 程式產生完成仍需驗收，不能直接推定可以上線。
外觀檢查無法證明異常、邊界與品質規則成立。
C：逐項執行對應驗收並保存實際證據；未測項目保留待驗。
換模型重新生成仍需相同驗收，無法取代測試。

en.prompt: AI has generated code from the specification and says every function is complete. What is the most reasonable next action?
options: Launch immediately
Check only visual appearance
Execute the corresponding normal, error and quality acceptance checks and retain evidence
Regenerate with a different AI model
rationales: Generated code still requires acceptance; it does not establish launch readiness.
Visual inspection cannot establish error, boundary or quality behavior.
C: Execute corresponding acceptance checks and preserve actual evidence; leave untested items unverified.
Regeneration with another model still requires the same acceptance tests.
